Intensive Multi-Cohort Assessment: Swine & Poultry Systems

Difficult_Example.Rmd

Advanced Assessment: Multi-Cohort Swine & Poultry Systems (Monogastric_Example)

This guide walks through an Advanced Multi-Cohort Assessment for monogastric livestock in Spain (swine and poultry), demonstrating how herdr models full pyramidal herd structures combining mature breeding stock, replacement rearing cohorts, and slaughter finishing cohorts within a single project.

📂 All files referenced below correspond to the pre-configured inst/Examples/Monogastric_Example/ dataset.

What you’ll edit

Category Files
User inputs (fill these in) livestock_census.csv · diet_profiles.csv · diet_ingredients.csv · monogastric_definitions.csv · livestock_weights.csv · manure_management.csv
Reference libraries (consult only) feed_characteristics.csv · mapping.csv · fao_crops.parquet · ipcc_coefficients.csv · ipcc_mm.csv · ecoalim.parquet

Step 1 — Multi-Cohort Census (livestock_census.csv)

In livestock_census.csv, we declare the Annual Average Population (AAP)—i.e., the average number of occupied barn places present on any given day of the year—for 10 cohorts across three distinct monogastric production enterprises on farm_1:

  1. Poultry Meat Enterprise (poultry / meat): broilers (slaughter), replacement_meat_pullets (replacement), and breeder_meat_hens (mature).
  2. Poultry Layer Enterprise (poultry / layer): replacement_layer_pullets (replacement), laying_hens (mature), and free_range_laying_hens (mature).
  3. Swine Meat Enterprise (swine / meat): fattening_pigs (slaughter), replacement_sows (replacement), breeder_sows (mature), and boars (mature).

Step 2 — Monogastric Definitions & Strict Role Taxonomy (monogastric_definitions.csv)

In monogastric_definitions.csv, every cohort is assigned:

  • animal_type: strictly poultry or swine.
  • animal_subtype:
    • For swine: strictly meat.
    • For poultry: strictly meat or layer.
  • production_role: strictly mature, replacement, or slaughter.

Step 3 — Weights & Batch Turnover (livestock_weights.csv)

For short-cycle monogastrics, productive_period_days controls both Average Daily Gain (ADG) for FEDNA Metabolizable Energy equations and annual batch turnover (365/productive_period_days365 / \text{productive\_period\_days}) for slaughter output:

  • broilers (slaughter): productive_period_days = 42 days (365/42≈8.69365 / 42 \approx 8.69 batches finished per barn place per year, from 0.044 kg to 2.60 kg).
  • fattening_pigs (slaughter): productive_period_days = 110 days (365/110≈3.32365 / 110 \approx 3.32 batches finished per barn place per year, from 20.0 kg to 111.82 kg).
  • breeder_sows (mature): productive_period_days = 148.9 days (farrowing interval, yielding 365/148.9≈2.45365 / 148.9 \approx 2.45 litters per sow per year), with sows_gestation_days = 115.1 and sows_lactation_days = 25.

Step 4 — How herdr Attributes Intensities in Table 2 (results$intensities)

When you run generate_impact_assessment(), herdr produces two complementary tables:

  1. Table 1 (results$totals): Shows the direct physical inventory of each of the 10 cohorts (enteric CH4\text{CH}_4, manure CH4\text{CH}_4, direct/indirect N2O\text{N}_2\text{O}, upstream feed fossil & LUC CO2e\text{CO}_2\text{e}, agroecological land, AWARE water, and per-head footprints).
  2. Table 2 (results$intensities): Computes enterprise-integrated product and protein intensities within each (farm_id, region, subregion, animal_type, animal_subtype) group:
    • Poultry Meat (poultry, meat): The overhead footprint of breeder_meat_hens (mature) and replacement_meat_pullets (replacement) is integrated with broilers (slaughter) over the total meat produced (broilers + culled breeders). replacement_meat_pullets shows NA for product intensities because its emissions are already absorbed into the meat enterprise.
    • Poultry Layers (poultry, layer): Each laying cohort (laying_hens and free_range_laying_hens) keeps its own direct footprint plus a population-proportional share (90% and 10%, respectively) of the replacement_layer_pullets overhead, divided by its respective egg production (egg_fresh_kg).
    • Swine Meat (swine, meat): The breeding herd overhead (breeder_sows + boars + replacement_sows) is integrated with fattening_pigs over total carcass pork output (finished pigs + culled sows/boars).

Step 5 — Running the Assessment & Visualizing Results 

library(herdr)

# Run assessment directly on the bundled Monogastric_Example
mono_dir <- system.file("Examples/Monogastric_Example", package = "herdr")

results <- generate_impact_assessment(
  data_dir        = mono_dir,
  automatic_cycle = FALSE,
  farm_country    = "Spain",
  year            = 2024,
  gwp_report      = "AR5",
  saveoutput      = FALSE
)

# Inspect Table 1 (Cohort Totals) and Table 2 (Enterprise Product Intensities)
results$totals
results$intensities

# 1. Compare Carbon Footprint per kg of Edible Protein across cohorts
plot_herdr_results(
  df              = results,
  group_cols      = "animal_tag",
  func_name       = "generate_impact_assessment",
  impact_category = "ghg",
  functional_unit = "protein"
)

# 2. Compare Egg Carbon Intensity between caged/barn vs. free-range hens
plot_herdr_results(
  df              = results,
  group_cols      = "animal_tag",
  func_name       = "generate_impact_assessment",
  impact_category = "ghg",
  functional_unit = "egg"
)
